chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog sent for hunting, which is named (over it), and it kills and eats from the prey, so he said: 'Eat, even if it eats from it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat from game hunted by a dog that ate some of it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the consumption of game is permissible even if the hunting dog eats from the prey, provided the hunter recites the name of Allah upon sending it. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that the dog's consumption does not nullify the sanctity of the hunt, distinguishing it from cases where the dog eats the entire prey or hunts without the initial invocation. The hadith highlights the practical flexibility in hunting laws, emphasizing the hunter's role in maintaining ritual purity through proper invocation rather than the dog's behavior alone.
